authority.basis: Applies the decision rule preregistered in gaia-research feat/ws-e-review-provenance-case commit 6d64bfb, recorded in results/v4/results.json and read back from the store. No threshold was chosen after any v4 result existed.

rationale:
Governed reading of five scored v4 pairs against the decision rule committed in gaia-research 6d64bfb before any arm ran. pairedDiscordance = 0 (|d| <= 1), so the rule selects `inconclusive`.

What the receipt shows: the treatment passed 1 of 5 pairs where control failed, and failed 1 of 5 where control passed. One discordant pair each way, no pooled effect, n=5.

What makes this inconclusive rather than merely null is the exposure record. The treatment skill body was actually read in 3 of 5 scored treatment arms. In the others the door listed it and the model never opened it, which the v3 lineage defines as listed-but-not-loaded and therefore not exposure. An effect measured on an arm that received no treatment is not evidence of no effect; it is evidence that this delivery design did not deliver reliably. Native-listing-with-on-demand-read is the suspect, not the skill.

Scope limits carried forward: one historically exposed case, so the model may have seen the public fix; n=5 cannot establish a general effect; the evaluator is not sandboxed from the agent's read tool. This case is single-skill and yields no interaction-edge finding under any outcome, so nothing here bears on gaia.arbor-edge/v1.

Consequence for consumers: this claim is NOT behavioral endorsement. A runtime may not treat the skill as behaviorally validated on the strength of this record, and the Tree must continue to project it as governed-but-unconfirmed.
